newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia economic adviser in talks for Sabah bank.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia economic adviser in talks for Sabah bank.

text.p: The Malaysian government's economic adviser Daim Zainuddin is in talks with the central bank to take over Hock Hua Bank (Sabah) Bhd, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Saturday.

Daim, who is a former finance minister, has been granted permission to open discussions with Bank Negara Malaysia for the takeover of the small commercial bank based in Malaysia's Borneo island state of Sabah, the national Bernama news agency quoted Anwar as saying.

The move did not contradict the government's desire for small banks to merge into larger entities, Anwar told reporters after officiating at the annual general meeting of the National Farmers Association (Nafas).
"The party taking over the bank must be able to upgrade the bank to Tier-1 status as soon as possible. If that condition is fulfilled, the takeover can continue," he said.
Under Malaysia's two-tier banking system, larger banks with shareholder funds of more than 500 million ringgit ($198.41 million) are classified as Tier-1.

Bank Negara has launched a drive to reduce the number of local commercial banks in the country from the present 24 through mergers to create fewer, larger units as the country opens its market to international competition.
Bernama said Anwar was commenting on a report in the Asian Wall Street Journal on Friday which said two business associates close to Daim were keen to take over Hock Hua Bank (Sabah).
The report said that the two, directors of UCM Industrial Corp Bhd Mohamed Nasir Ali and Lutfiah Ismail, have obtained regulatory approval to make on offer to buy the bank.

Hock Hua Bank (Sabah) has 12 branches in the state and is a 70.7 percent-owned subsidiary of Hock Hua Bank Bhd. The Hock Hua Bank group based in Sarawak is controlled by timber and trading tycoon Ling Beng Siew.
The bank is the 16th largest commercial bank in Malaysia in terms of shareholders funds. Hock Hua Bank (Sabah) is the smallest. ($1=2.52 ringgit)
